scope: Full frozen v13 raw-data crosscheck, no new engine edits/builds/game runs during report update. Historical paired/decoded v12 native proofs preserved separately.

historical_v3.scope: Historical read-only classification of full v3 data, before arithmetic and later broad-phase/ray fixes; not the final candidate counters.
historical_v3.small_sphere_policy: Only normals for 0.1 <= radius <= 1 cm (1–10 mm) are accepted by the user; points, hits, material and sector retain the original gates.

both_engines_failed_center_ray_fallback.evidence: Public result fraction is exactly 1 while hasHit is true; both implementations reset fraction only when attempting the center ray, and any successful center ray would have fraction < 1.

proven_arithmetic_difference.cause: Float32 blend (1-t)*from+t*to and affine from+(to-from)*t differ under large extrapolation. The saved outputs are exactly reproduced at their exported precision.
proven_arithmetic_difference.minimal_fix: Preserve the old public sweep fraction and interpolation expressions; retain Jolt hit detection and native normals.

unknowns: IDs 7157/12169/37252: output data cannot distinguish Bullet missing the upper sphere candidate from different legacy center-ray fallback decisions.
Coincident projected bottom points do not prove coincident geometry or identical native contacts; initial overlap maps different candidate contacts to the same public point.

candidate_minimal_fix_requiring_trace.cause: Bullet accepts an initial separation up to its 1 mm conservative advancement stopping distance; Jolt sphere geometry does not add that tolerance. May explain some Bullet-only initial contacts but saved outputs do not prove distance to the geometry.
candidate_minimal_fix_requiring_trace.caution: Do not inflate all sphere casts or waive hits: that changes positive time-of-impact points. Trace actual initial separation first.

historical_v10.scope: Historical full v10 raw-data crosscheck; superseded by v11. All earlier mismatches remain recorded here.

both_engines_failed_center_ray_fallback.evidence: Both saved results have hit=true and fraction=1; public points are away from the segment endpoint. The wrapper resets only fraction after a failed center ray, so these retain sphere results. This classifies the wrapper branch, not the native cause of each mismatch.

confirmed_reference_public_sphere_false_.proof: Both engines and, crucially, the original Bullet center ray intersect a surface strictly inside the same center segment and under the same landscape/object category filter. A sphere of positive radius necessarily intersects that surface when its center reaches the ray witness. The original public sphere query therefore misses an actual intersection. This does not prove which native solver or wrapper branch missed it, or that Jolt selected the exact first contact/metadata. No waiver is added.

corrected_point_disagreements_v10_to_v11.status: Source-plane refinement of the ray wrapper removed these public sphere point differences; all are ray-equivalent outputs in both snapshots, consistent with the center-ray fallback. No sphere solver has been copied or reintroduced.

remaining_ray_equivalent_point_differenc.status: Every exported sphere field is identical to the same-engine ordinary ray result. These point deltas are also the three remaining ordinary-ray deltas, rather than independent evidence of a sphere solver defect. Without native contact traces, exact fallback versus coincident projection is not asserted.

preserved_legacy_projection_defect.proof: The common public point lies about 18.03 km from the center segment, outside its radius-100cm swept volume. It is the legacy bottom-height projection onto an extrapolated center line, not a physical contact point. Both backends retain this semantic artifact; it is not a Jolt regression or a reason to waive other fields.

small_normal_domain_sanity.scope: A sanity check of the reported normal domain, not proof of every underlying contact. No hits, points or metadata are exempted.

new_adapter_defects_proven_from_remainin.status: No new adapter defect is established from remaining public raw sphere outputs alone. This is absence of proof, not a claim that the adapter is correct.

source_semantics.initial_overlap_tie_rule: Native BVH traversal and equal-fraction candidate choice can differ; coincident projected public points do not identify the same primitive.
source_semantics.zero_object_normal_semantics: DynamicWorld::toResult intentionally exports zero normals for object bodies, so a zero public normal does not prove an invalid native contact.

historically_unresolved_19_hit_disagreem.status: Original triangle vertices/IDs and native cast contacts are absent; baseline false positives versus Jolt adapter/native misses cannot be distinguished.
